need.text: sample demo dates "must roll with the current day", with "now" anchored once per demo session. DECISIONS.md wording: "Sample data dates keep rolling with the current day; anchor 'now' once per demo session so counts stay stable during a run." Acceptance in C-386: counts are stable across midnight UTC. Authoritative inputs: the demo sample-data dates; the session clock.

acceptance.statement: The kernel exports dayStartMs, sampleDateMs, daysAgo and inWindow, and imports nothing.

check.run: grep -q 'export function dayStartMs' /in/compose/kernel.ts && grep -q 'export function sampleDateMs' /in/compose/kernel.ts && grep -q 'export function daysAgo' /in/compose/kernel.ts && grep -q 'export function inWindow' /in/compose/kernel.ts && ! grep -Eq '^\s*import ' /in/compose/kernel.ts

acceptance.statement: All four artefact files exist and tests.json and glue.json are valid JSON.
Gates G1-G7 all pass on the composed artefact.

Counts are stable across midnight UTC: with one anchor fixed, results of sampleDateMs, daysAgo and inWindow do not depend on any other clock reading. The kernel takes the anchor as an argument and never reads a clock. Tests cover an anchor at 23:59:59.999 UTC and a later 'now' just past midnight with the same anchor.
Sample dates roll with the current day: for two anchors on different UTC days, the same (daysAgo, msIntoDay) arguments produce dates shifted by exactly the difference in days.

check.criteria: tests.json contains calls to sampleDateMs with two anchors one or more UTC days apart and expected values differing by exactly that many days times 86400000.

acceptance.statement: CONTRACT.md states the assumption taken (UTC day boundary, sample dates never later than the anchor day, the host captures the anchor once per session and passes it in), the one question that resolves the open fact, and which inputs are refused.

check.criteria: CONTRACT.md has an explicit assumption, exactly one question, and a list of refused inputs matching the traps in tests.json and glue.json.

worker.prompt: Define the interface of a pure numeric kernel that makes demo sample dates roll with the current UTC day from a once-per-session anchor. Use the four exports named in the contract. The kernel never reads a clock; the anchor is an argument. Give names, argument names, units, return types and the trap conditions for each export.

atoms.title: Contract with assumption and question
atoms.contract: CONTRACT.md states what each export computes, the assumption taken for open facts, exactly one question that resolves it, and the refused inputs.
atoms.verify: grep for headings Computes, Assumption, Question, Refused; question count is 1

worker.prompt: Write CONTRACT.md. State: day boundary is UTC midnight (the request's acceptance names midnight UTC); the anchor is captured once per session by the host and passed in; sample dates are anchor-day start minus daysAgo days plus msIntoDay, never later than the anchor day. The open fact is whether sample data may include future-dated entries and what maximum age is wanted; take the assumption (no future dates, max 3650 days, windowDays 1..3650) and ask one question that resolves it. List refused inputs: non-finite or negative timestamps, daysAgo outside 0..3650, msIntoDay outside 0..86399999, windowDays outside 1..3650, an event on a later UTC day than the anchor. Do not invent facts about the equipment.
